title: Max Finks, back to Chicago, the Mary Garden, Chicago Theater and Meroff
summary: He recalls Liberty and the Palace, then Chicago dance halls and night clubs, the Chicago Theater pit and stage bands, and playing for Benny Meroff.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: Yeah. But, well, did you ever play at the Orpheum?
No, I never did. The Palace Theater. I played Liberty with Max Finks. Do you remember? You heard Max Finks?
I heard of him. I never knew him. He was before I ever got here.

He was terrific. Good showman and all that stuff. But, like I say, I went to Chicago and I came back to New Orleans. I went back to the Palace. But I just wanted to go back to, you know, out of town, so I went back to Chicago. So, I went back there and I played the dance hall, like the Mary Garden. That was a big deal. And, who happened to have two dance halls ones? It was like a T. And, uh, Paul Moreas and George Abrunas, they played with the other band, Ben Pollack, you know, and all that stuff. That's where that band started out. This was at the Mary Garden. Mary Garden, yeah. That's on an art sign. I think it was on Crawford. So, I played a few night club, like the Green Mill, that was where the Tiberi Theater is now, up on, have you been in Chicago? Not in a long time. Well, you know where the Tiberi Theater is now, up on, and I think. I remember it kind of vaguely. You know where Lawrence Avenue.
I know where the Drake Hotel is. That's about all I can remember now. It's been so many years ago. Oh, yeah. Oh, yeah.

And then, uh, I started playing Waterville. Went back to Waterville. I played with the Chicago Theater with a 50-piece band, you know, in the pit. And then, uh, we had stage presentation on stage after we got finished playing the pit band. That was a 25-piece band on the stage. So, I stayed there quite a while, but a little over 10 years. And then, uh, I played with Benny, uh, Benny Miroff. You heard of Benny Miroff?
Yeah. I heard his records, anyway. Huh?

He made some records with Wild Bill, you know. Yeah, Wild Bill did. He played with the band. That's right. Maury Stein, the writer on Hollywood, was writing a lot of tunes, you know. He writes a lot of tunes.
